page: Amazon Web Services x2idn.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a dedicated 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor featuring the x86_64 architecture, configured with 32 physical cores and 64 virtual cores across 2 threads per core. The compute hardware is backed by 54 MB of L3 cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and supports instruction extensions including AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance contains no dedicated GPUs, but bundles 1900 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and delivers 50 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth.

A primary architectural feature of the x2idn.16xlarge is its massive memory density, offering 1024 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, translating to an expansive 16:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio (16 GB per virtual core). This generous allocation supports large-scale in-memory operational workloads without relying on external block storage caching. In synthetic and functional benchmarks, the instance demonstrates strong multi-core processing power, ranking in the top 25 percent in stress-ng multi-core CPU testing (61,925.72), PassMark CPU score (56,725.09), and PassMark database operations (26,134.77). Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 81.72 GB/sec, while static web serving throughput measures 46.18 GB/sec.

Single-core performance profiles within the middle 50 percent, reflecting standard per-core execution speeds rather than ultra-high burst clock frequencies. Memory bandwidth throughput similarly places in average tiers, yielding 166.56 GB/sec for uncached read operations. The inclusion of high-speed local NVMe storage combined with heavy memory capacity provides significant resource efficiency for organizations needing enterprise-scale memory footprints alongside high local I/O performance on standard Intel architecture.

Given its hardware specifications and benchmark results, the x2idn.16xlarge is optimal for in-memory databases like SAP HANA or Redis clusters, real-time analytics, large-scale ETL processing, and memory-bound transactional databases requiring fast local scratch storage and high networking capability.
